To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NLR, PLR and AISI are not associated with AMD in men, and the ability of AISR and MPV to identify AMD is poor.
the ability of the investigated inflammation markers to discriminate between men with AMD and age-matched cataract controls is poor.

neutrophil/ lymphocyte ratio, derived neutrophil/ white blood cells ratio, platelet/ lymphocyte ratio and monocyte/lympthocyte ratio are not associated with age related macular degeration (AMD) in men.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of some inflammatory biomarkers, which can be derived from the blood count, in the pathogenesis of late-stage AMD.
the role of inflammation in the development and progression of age related macular disease.
the role of blood cell count derived inflammation biomarker in age related macula degeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NLR, PLR and MLR are unreliable inflammation biomarkers in AMD patients.
NLR, PLR and AISI are not useful biomarkers of AMD.
the blood count derived inflammatory biomarkers investigated in this study do not seem to play a role in AMD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the blood cell count derived inflammation biomarker, AISI, is significantly lower in men with late stage, exudative AMD compared with cataract controls.
the blood cell count derived inflammation biomarker values are not reliable disease biomarkers in late stage AMD patients.
the blood count derived inflammation markers are not reliable biomarkers in men.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined inflammation biomarkers are not reliable biomarkers in men.
the blood count derived inflammation markers are not reliable biomarkers of AMD in men.
AISI and MPVL are poor disease biomarkers in AMD.
